scenes.visual: Title card: When the Division Is Rigged.

scenes.tts: What happens when a neuroblast fails to sort its cargo? And why can one small error grow so large?
scenes.visual: A neuroblast dividing with its cargo scattered. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: What happens when a neuroblast fails to sort its cargo? And why can one small error grow so large?

scenes.tts: In two thousand five, Emmanuel Caussinus and Cayetano Gonzalez ran a transplant test.
scenes.caption: In 2005, Emmanuel Caussinus and Cayetano Gonzalez ran a transplant test.
scenes.visual: Name card: Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005.
scenes.narration: In 2005, Emmanuel Caussinus and Cayetano Gonzalez ran a transplant test.

scenes.tts: They put larval brain tissue from pins, miranda, numb or prospero mutants into adult flies.
scenes.visual: A larval brain with four gene labels: pins, miranda, numb, prospero.
scenes.narration: They put larval brain tissue from pins, miranda, numb or prospero mutants into adult flies.

scenes.tts: The tissue grew to more than a hundred times its starting size. It invaded other tissues and killed its hosts.
scenes.visual: The tissue swells. On screen: more than 100 times starting size. Arrows show invasion into other tissues.
scenes.narration: The tissue grew to more than a hundred times its starting size. It invaded other tissues and killed its hosts.

scenes.visual: Hold on the reveal.

scenes.tts: In two thousand six, Yorg Betschinger, Karl Mechtler and Yurgen Knoblich studied Brat and Prospero.
scenes.caption: In 2006, Jörg Betschinger, Karl Mechtler and Jürgen Knoblich studied Brat and Prospero.
scenes.visual: Name card: Betschinger, Mechtler and Knoblich, 2006.
scenes.narration: In 2006, Jörg Betschinger, Karl Mechtler and Jürgen Knoblich studied Brat and Prospero.

scenes.tts: In brat or prospero mutants, both daughters grew like neuroblasts and formed brain tumours.
scenes.visual: Two timelines. Prospero mutant, type I lineage: a GMC fails to differentiate and keeps dividing. Brat mutant, type II lineage: an immature intermediate progenitor fails to mature and takes on neuroblast identity. Only then do both timelines end in a tumour mass.
scenes.narration: In brat or prospero mutants, both daughters grew like neuroblasts and formed brain tumours.

scenes.tts: Later work showed the two guard different cells. Brat tumours arise mainly in type two lineages, from intermediate progenitors that fail to mature.
scenes.caption: Later work showed the two guard different cells. Brat tumours arise mainly in type II lineages, from intermediate progenitors that fail to mature.
scenes.visual: Brat guards the intermediate progenitor of a type II lineage; without it, immature progenitors fail to mature and can take on neuroblast identity.
scenes.narration: Later work showed the two guard different cells. Brat tumours arise mainly in type II lineages, from intermediate progenitors that fail to mature.

scenes.tts: Prospero tumours arise from ganglion mother cells.
scenes.visual: Prospero guards the GMC; without it, GMCs keep dividing.
scenes.narration: Prospero tumours arise from ganglion mother cells.

scenes.tts: But how can a small leak at every division grow more than a hundredfold?
scenes.visual: Card: an illustrative model, not a measurement.
scenes.narration: But how can a small leak at every division grow more than a hundredfold?

scenes.tts: Take one neuroblast that divides once per round. With perfect sorting, each small daughter becomes a ganglion mother cell.
scenes.visual: One neuroblast and a round counter. Each round adds one GMC beside it.
scenes.narration: Take one neuroblast that divides once per round. With perfect sorting, each small daughter becomes a ganglion mother cell.

scenes.tts: With leaky sorting, each small daughter has a chance, f, of staying a neuroblast. Every neuroblast divides in the next round.
scenes.visual: Some small daughters turn into neuroblasts. Symbol on screen: f, the fraction that leaks each round.
scenes.narration: With leaky sorting, each small daughter has a chance, f, of staying a neuroblast. Every neuroblast divides in the next round.

scenes.tts: Run fifty rounds. How many neuroblasts with perfect sorting? How many if one small daughter in ten stays a neuroblast?
scenes.caption: Run 50 rounds. How many neuroblasts with perfect sorting? How many if one small daughter in ten stays a neuroblast?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: 50 rounds; f = 0 and f = 0.10. Two blank counters.
scenes.narration: Run 50 rounds. How many neuroblasts with perfect sorting? How many if one small daughter in ten stays a neuroblast?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: With perfect sorting, there is still one neuroblast. Its output just adds up, round by round.
scenes.visual: Counter: 1 neuroblast. Output counter: 50 GMCs produced over 50 rounds, then 100 neurons or glia if every GMC divides once and all survive. A straight line labelled cumulative progeny rises slowly.
scenes.narration: With perfect sorting, there is still one neuroblast. Its output just adds up, round by round.

scenes.tts: With the leak, the neuroblasts multiply every round, on average. The count compounds.
scenes.visual: Counter for f = 0.10 climbs faster and faster. On screen: the average number of neuroblasts multiplies by (1 + f) each round.
scenes.narration: With the leak, the neuroblasts multiply every round, on average. The count compounds.

scenes.tts: With one in ten leaking, the average passes a hundred neuroblasts after fifty rounds.
scenes.caption: With one in ten leaking, the average passes a hundred neuroblasts after 50 rounds.
scenes.visual: Table headed: average neuroblasts, starting from 1, after 25 and 50 rounds. f = 0, 1 and 1; f = 0.02, 1.6 and 2.7; f = 0.05, 3.4 and 11.5; f = 0.10, 10.8 and 117; f = 0.20, 95 and 9,100. Labels: illustrative model; single lineages vary.
scenes.narration: With one in ten leaking, the average passes a hundred neuroblasts after 50 rounds.

scenes.visual: Hold on the reveal.

scenes.tts: These round counts are illustrative, not measured. The model counts neuroblasts, not tissue size. It is not a fit to the transplant data.
scenes.visual: Labels stay on screen: illustrative round counts; counts neuroblasts, not tissue size; not a fit to the transplant data.
scenes.narration: These round counts are illustrative, not measured. The model counts neuroblasts, not tissue size. It is not a fit to the transplant data.

scenes.tts: It shows only that a small leak at each division, compounded, can multiply the dividing cells more than a hundredfold.
scenes.visual: Axes: rounds; average neuroblast count, starting from 1. The f = 0.10 curve crosses a line labelled 100 times the starting neuroblast count.
scenes.narration: It shows only that a small leak at each division, compounded, can multiply the dividing cells more than a hundredfold.

scenes.tts: In mammals, the picture is less clear. Mice have Numb and a second relative, Numblike.
scenes.visual: A mouse embryo cortex. Labels: Numb, Numblike.
scenes.narration: In mammals, the picture is less clear. Mice have Numb and a second relative, Numblike.

scenes.tts: Removing both early in the nervous system used up progenitors.
scenes.visual: Two-row table, row 1: Petersen and colleagues, 2002; nervous system; early; progenitors used up.
scenes.narration: Removing both early in the nervous system used up progenitors.

scenes.tts: Removing both in the dorsal forebrain, studied across the later peak of neurogenesis, made progenitors overproliferate.
scenes.visual: Row 2: Li and colleagues, 2003; dorsal forebrain; from E9.5; progenitors overproliferate.
scenes.narration: Removing both in the dorsal forebrain, studied across the later peak of neurogenesis, made progenitors overproliferate.

scenes.tts: The two studies differ in where and when Numb was removed. Which difference matters is not settled.
scenes.visual: The where and when columns of the two-row table highlight. A question mark sits beside them.
scenes.narration: The two studies differ in where and when Numb was removed. Which difference matters is not settled.

scenes.tts: Numb also has other jobs in these cells. So a mouse phenotype is not automatically a Notch veto.
scenes.visual: Icons for Numb's other jobs: junctions between progenitors, and endocytosis.
scenes.narration: Numb also has other jobs in these cells. So a mouse phenotype is not automatically a Notch veto.

scenes.tts: One question points onward. Numb makes two sisters different. It does not say which of many neuron types they become.
scenes.visual: A GMC's progeny with many possible neuron-type labels hovering above them.
scenes.narration: One question points onward. Numb makes two sisters different. It does not say which of many neuron types they become.

scenes.tts: That depends on when a cell was born, the subject of the next lesson.
scenes.visual: Link card: birth order and fate.
scenes.narration: That depends on when a cell was born, the subject of the next lesson.

scenes.tts: A rigged division leaks self-renewal into the wrong daughter. Compounded, a small leak can multiply the dividing cells.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: sorting failure leaks self-renewal; the leak compounds.
scenes.narration: A rigged division leaks self-renewal into the wrong daughter. Compounded, a small leak can multiply the dividing cells.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
